::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Prove that every point of $f(x)$ is on a linear function](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3224655/prove-that-every-point-of-fx-is-on-a-linear-function), asked by [Ori](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/671368/ori) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2019-05-13; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> $f(x)$ is continuous on [0,1]. Every point $(x,f(x)), x\in \Bbb Q$ is on the linear function $y=(f(1)-f(0))x+f(0)$.
> Prove that every point $(r,f(r))$ (when $r$ is irrational) is on this linear function.
:::

Your problem is essentially equivalent to this one:

> Let $f$ and $g$ be continuous functions with $f(x) = g(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Q}$. Show that $f(x) = g(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Obviously, the continuity condition is really important.  The other property that's used is the [density](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1027970/what-does-it-mean-for-rational-numbers-to-be-dense-in-the-reals) of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$.
